summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and chronic hepatitis C was admitted for acute chest and left leg pain consistent with a vaso-occlusive crisis. She had uncontrolled pain despite home oral Dilaudid, requiring IV analgesia. Chest X-ray showed chronic interstitial changes without acute findings, ruling out acute chest syndrome. Tibia/fibula imaging revealed no fracture or new infarct, with tenderness attributed to a hematoma. Pain improved with IV then oral medications. Her home regimen was adjusted at discharge to include scheduled acetaminophen and naproxen to reduce reliance on opioids, with continued monitoring of proteinuria and hepatitis C. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions for early follow-up.
problems: Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
